fields.narrative_intro: *A grimacing person and a swaggering person discuss Project Suncatcher on a Zoom call where nobody can hear you.*
fields.panel1:
[setup]
GRIMACING PERSON: "Google's Project Suncatcher puts Trillium TPUs in orbit."
SWAGGERING PERSON: "Earth ran out of places to run machine learning."
fields.panel2:
[build]
SWAGGERING PERSON: "Transporter-18 rideshare: SpaceX, Planet, and up to eight times more solar power."
GRIMACING PERSON: "So the data center is going solar by leaving Earth."
fields.panel3:
[pivot]
GRIMACING PERSON: "Crocker Nuclear Laboratory simulates five years' radiation; launches hit 50–100g."
SWAGGERING PERSON: "Then high-bandwidth lasers hit coin-sized targets while everything moves."
fields.panel4:
[silent reaction]
[Visual: Both stare at a silent Zoom window; an orbital laser misses a coin-sized mute icon.]
fields.panel5:
[punch]
SWAGGERING PERSON: "How do they explain missing the 2027 deadline?"
GRIMACING PERSON: "The deadline was a moving, coin-sized target."
fields.panel6:
[button]
[Visual: The laser hits the mute icon perfectly; a calendar marked 2027 drifts past.]

narrative_summary: The orbital data center's escalating engineering demands turn its 2027 deadline into another moving, coin-sized target—and Zoom is still muted.
rationale: Candidate 3 uses the story’s specific engineering details while finding a fresher angle in the 2027 deadline becoming a moving, coin-sized target. Its punchline escalates the laser-targeting premise rather than simply repeating the familiar “we can’t hit Unmute” joke.
story_title: Google’s Project Suncatcher to put ML infrastructure in space
place: on a Zoom call where nobody can hear you
hat_pair: foam binoculars worn as an oversized hat with two giant lens holes staring outward
dunce cap with the word SMART scrawled on it in marker
